content: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Cefepime is a medication used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as cephalosporin antibiotics. This medication is administered via injection into a muscle or vein as directed by your doctor. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you have been properly instructed by your healthcare provider on how to prepare and administer it. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. If using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the bag at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the bag well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the bag leaks. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using cefepime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other antibiotics (such as penicillins or other cephalosporins), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefepime may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). This medication passes into breast milk in small amounts and is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (including some urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as complete blood count and kidney function tests) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
